headline: Selling Swamps the Tape as Only Energy Holds Its Ground
body_html:
Thursday's session ended with sellers firmly in charge. Of the 668 stocks we track, 484 fell and just 180 rose, so barely more than a quarter of the list finished higher. Energy was the only sector to close in positive territory, up 0.13%, and even that gain was slight.

The rotation ran toward the oil patch and away from rate-sensitive and consumer-facing groups. Homebuilders fared worst, down 2.72%, followed by consumer names at 2.11%. Financials lost 1.23%, healthcare and materials each gave up 1.17%, and semiconductors, industrials and software slipped between 0.57% and 0.83%. Pockets of strength were scarce: DPC Holdings climbed 8.48%, Installed Building Products rose 6.71%, HubSpot added 6.32% and AMD gained 5.86%.

The session's standout mover was Corteva, which fell 24.3%, the steepest drop on our board by a wide margin. Cellebrite lost 14.25%, Digi International 12.72%, Warby Parker 11.31% and YETI 10.42%. With Friday's session next, the day's lesson is simple: when selling is this widespread, a handful of strong gainers cannot offset it, and the sharpest damage landed on individual names.

briefs.headline: Cloud Outage Disrupts Email and Web Services
briefs.body: A Microsoft outage knocked out Outlook on Thursday, and users of Amazon's and Google's cloud services also reported problems. The episode is a reminder of how much business activity depends on a few large providers. Details on the cause and duration were not part of the reports.

briefs.headline: United Draws a Line on AI Booking Bots
briefs.body: United Airlines will not let AI agents book flights for customers. One expert argued travelers would be wise not to hand that task to a bot anyway. The stance shows how carriers are weighing automation against control of the customer relationship.

briefs.headline: Trump Signals No Rush on an Iran Deal
briefs.body: President Trump said the U.S. does not need a deal with Iran and told Vice President Vance to focus on domestic corruption. Separately, a UK court found two Iranian men guilty of helping Iranian intelligence. Both stories add to the geopolitical backdrop for energy traders.

briefs.headline: Fed Changes Course on a Far-Off Meeting
briefs.body: In a policy switch, the Federal Reserve said its October 2027 meeting will not include a vote on interest rates. The change is nearly a year away, so it has no immediate effect on pricing. It does show the central bank is still adjusting how it schedules its decisions.

briefs.headline: Red Sea Tensions Hit Oil Infrastructure
briefs.body: Yemen's Houthis said they attacked a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline. Separately, a tanker was struck off the coast of Ras Al-Khaimah in the UAE, and all crew were reported safe. Energy was the only sector to finish higher on Thursday.

briefs.headline: Trump Jr. Steps Back From Kalshi Role
briefs.body: Donald Trump Jr. has left his advisory role at the prediction market Kalshi. The exit comes as such platforms draw growing attention from regulators and politicians. No reason for the departure was given in the reports we reviewed.
